Today’s M&A briefing — 21 deals, the strategies behind them · 5 November 2026

🔹 Alcatel Submarine Networks (ASN) (manufacturing, laying, and maintenance of submarine cable systems) acquires Ship As A Service (SAAS) (marine geophysical prospecting, vessel fleet, ROV piloting).

🔹 TRA-C industrie (engineering and industrial subcontracting — welding, machining) acquires MécaSup (precision machining and manufacturing of high-value technical parts).

🔹 Indy (all-in-one accounting, professional account) acquires Dotnet (fiche-paie.net online payroll software for VSEs and freelancers).

🔹 Accès Industrie (rental of lifting and handling equipment, France) acquires Atlas Rental (rental of lifting equipment primarily for construction and industry).

🔹 Optio Group (managing General Agent, MGA specializing in niche insurance) acquires Names Europe Agencia de Suscripción (underwriting complex marine and transport risks in the Spanish market).

🔹 FSN Capital VI (nordic private equity fund, thesis focused on safety and security) acquires Zenitel (critical communication solutions — intercom, public address).

🔹 Pactic (european logistics and e-commerce fulfillment) acquires QeOPS (warehouse management and e-commerce fulfillment, Romania).

🔹 MBA Surgical Empowerment (medico-surgical technology — orthopedics, spine, neurosurgery) acquires MoonSurge Importação e Exportação de Material Médico (distribution of medical devices).

🔹 Orbus International B.V (medical devices for angioplasty and percutaneous coronary intervention) acquires MC Health (import, distribution, and sale of medical devices for cardiovascular).

🔹 Sacmi (via Protesa) (imola industrial cooperative) acquires 80 % de ST Powertrain (failure analysis, testing, and quality control for high-end automotive).

🔹 Infitech (parent company of Fonds Finanz) acquires 75,1 % de Kees Finanzberater.

🔹 Quercus TFI (polish asset manager, distributor of financial products via Xelion DI) acquires 49 % d'Open Life (life insurance, Poland, resulting from liquidation).

🔹 Logson Group (independent corrugated packaging manufacturer, Coalville) acquires Playford Packaging (corrugated sheet manufacturing, Wrexham, North Wales, founded in 1980).

🔹 Dubbeldam Industries (network of specialists in bodywork, hydraulics, repair, and service) acquires Van den Born Carrosserie (custom outfitting, conversion).

🔹 Dutech Holdings (owner of bicycle brands Batavus, KOGA, Carqon, XLC, and Babboe) takes over Juncker Bike Parts (Accell Nederland) business (distribution of bicycle parts and accessories).

🔹 FSN Capital VI (fonds de private equity nordique) rachète Zenitel (solutions de communication critique — interphonie, sonorisation).

🔹 Quercus TFI (gestionnaire d'actifs polonais, distributeur de produits financiers) rachète 49 % d'Open Life (assurance-vie, Pologne, issue d'une liquidation judiciaire).

🔹 Logson Group (fabricant indépendant d'emballages en carton ondulé, Coalville) acquiert Playford Packaging (fabrication de feuilles de carton ondulé, Wrexham).

🔹 Dubbeldam Industries (réseau de spécialistes en carrosserie, hydraulique) acquiert Van den Born Carrosserie (aménagement, transformation et équipement sur mesure de véhicules utilitaires légers pour collectivités, État et gestionnaires de flottes, Waalwijk).

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 3 deals, the strategies behind them · 5 November 2026

🔹 Pliant (modular B2B payments platform — commercial cards, payment accounts, currency exchange, expense management, native AI agents) — $80m · Series C.
Pliant is a principal member of Visa and Mastercard, issues cards in 32 countries and 13 currencies under a European e-money license. It allows third-party AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT) to trigger payments via the MCP protocol.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Expansion into the United States and Canada, entry into new international markets, acceleration of the AI roadmap.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Seaya Nova and Speedinvest (co-leads); Illuminate Financial, Motive Partners, Molten Ventures (participants).
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Where most expense management solutions treat AI as an added analytical layer, Pliant builds an infrastructure where AI agents directly execute payments — a bet on value capture at execution rather than analysis.

🔹 Titan OS (independent Linux operating system for smart TVs, advertising revenue sharing model with manufacturers, Barcelona) — €40m.
Founded in 2023 by Jacinto Roca (former founder of Wuaki.tv, acquired by Rakuten). Partner manufacturers include Philips and JVC. Total funding since inception: €97 M. The company is already present in millions of homes.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Highland Europe and Mangrove Capital Partners (existing investors); credit facility from funds managed by BlackRock.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Titan OS's model is that of a distribution infrastructure with a double network effect: the more manufacturers adopt the OS, the larger the audience grows, the more advertisers pay, and the more shared revenue attracts new manufacturers.

🔹 CyberKord (AI platform for IT and security operations automation — from alert to remediation — with digital twin testing before application) — €2.7m · Pre-seed.
Founded in 2026 by Alessandro Maggio, Dragos Tanasa, and Cosimo Michelagnoli. The platform connects to existing cloud and on-premise systems without replacement and allows the client to control the degree of autonomy granted to the AI.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: 360 Capital (lead); Plus Partners, Addendum Capital, Vento (participants).
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The digital twin that absorbs testing risk before any real action is the direct answer to the main impediment to security automation: the fear of breaking something in production.

fr.text:
Levées de fonds : les 3 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 5 novembre 2026.

🔹 Pliant (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑙𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑖𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝐵2𝐵 — 𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑒𝑠 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑚𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑒𝑠, 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑝𝑡𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑖𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡, 𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑔𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑒𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑒𝑠, 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑒𝑠) — 80 M$ · Série C.
Pliant est membre principal de Visa et Mastercard, émet des cartes dans 32 pays et 13 devises sous licence monnaie électronique européenne. Elle permet à des agents IA tiers (Claude, ChatGPT) de déclencher des paiements via le protocole MCP.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Expansion aux États-Unis et au Canada, entrée sur de nouveaux marchés internationaux, accélération de la feuille de route IA.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Seaya Nova et Speedinvest (co-leads) ; Illuminate Financial, Motive Partners, Molten Ventures (participants).
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Là où la plupart des solutions de gestion des dépenses traitent l'IA comme une couche d'analyse ajoutée, Pliant construit une infrastructure où les agents IA exécutent directement les paiements — un pari sur la capture de valeur à l'exécution plutôt qu'à l'analyse.

🔹 Titan OS (𝑠𝑦𝑠𝑡𝑒̀𝑚𝑒 𝑑'𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝐿𝑖𝑛𝑢𝑥 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑒𝑛𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑡𝑒́𝑙𝑒́𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑒́𝑠, 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑒̀𝑙𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑟𝑒𝑣𝑒𝑛𝑢𝑠 𝑝𝑢𝑏𝑙𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑣𝑒𝑐 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑓𝑎𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑠) — 40 M€.
Fondée en 2023 par Jacinto Roca (ex-fondateur de Wuaki.tv, acquis par Rakuten). Fabricants partenaires incluent Philips et JVC. Financement total depuis la création : 97 M€. La société est déjà présente dans des millions de foyers.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Highland Europe et Mangrove Capital Partners (investisseurs existants) ; facilité de crédit de fonds gérés par BlackRock.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Le modèle de Titan OS est celui d'une infrastructure de distribution à double effet de réseau : plus de fabricants adoptent l'OS, plus l'audience grandit, plus les annonceurs paient, plus les revenus partagés attirent de nouveaux fabricants.

🔹 CyberKord (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝐼𝐴 𝑑'𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝐼𝑇 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑒́𝑐𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑒́ — 𝑑𝑒 𝑙'𝑎𝑙𝑒𝑟𝑡𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝑙𝑎 𝑐𝑜𝑟𝑟𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛) — 2,7 M€ · Pré-seed.
Fondée en 2026 par Alessandro Maggio, Dragos Tanasa et Cosimo Michelagnoli. La plateforme se connecte aux systèmes cloud et on-premise existants sans remplacement et laisse au client le contrôle du degré d'autonomie accordé à l'IA.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : 360 Capital (lead) ; Plus Partners, Addendum Capital, Vento (participants).
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Le jumeau numérique qui absorbe le risque du test avant toute action réelle est la réponse directe au principal frein à l'automatisation en sécurité : la peur de casser quelque chose en production.
